propositions: Fixed-count folding threshold (T=10) creates superlinear Θ(N²) retained snapshot bytes as large tickets grow, despite I1 append-only retention of sources.

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence (fold when pending_source_bytes >= alpha * active_snapshot_bytes) reduces retained-snapshot bytes from Θ(N²) to Θ(N) with measured 344× reduction at N=8,000 events while bounding replay cost to alpha times snapshot size.

Current compaction policy violates ADR 0035 contracts (conservative horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, two-clone union safety) only in WHEN folds trigger, not snapshot placement or retire/restore rules, so all cadence candidates preserve safety invariants.

Byte-cost candidate requires configuration knob (compact.snapshot_alpha, default ≤0 for backward compatibility), optional adoption per ticket, and dedicated two-clone reconvergence test before production deployment.
